title: The Five Laws of SE for AI

edges.target: Hidden technical debt in ML systems (Sculley et al.) - Google LOC diagram
edges.ref: 7. D. Sculley et al., "Hidden technical debt in machine learning systems," in Proc. 28th Int. Conf. Neural Information Processing Systems, vol. 2, pp. 2503-2511.
edges.evidence: David Sculley offered Figure 3, which represents the size (in lines of code) of Google's software suite. Note how small the AI box is
edges.section: Rule 1: AI Software Mostly Isn't About AI (Figure 3)

edges.target: Hidden technical debt in ML systems (Sculley et al.) - data-dictionary coupling anecdote
edges.ref: 7. D. Sculley et al., "Hidden technical debt in machine learning systems," in Proc. 28th Int. Conf. Neural Information Processing Systems, vol. 2, pp. 2503-2511.
edges.evidence: Sculley's 2015 talk offers us an example. He reported that Google's machine-learning developers used all of the attributes in the company's data dictionaries
edges.section: Rule 3: Poor SE Leads to Poor AI

edges.target: Microsoft nine-step ML pipeline (Amershi et al.)
edges.ref: 8. S. Amershi et al., "Software engineering for machine learning: A case study," in Proc. 41st Int. Conf. Software Engineering: SEIP '19, pp. 291-300.
edges.evidence: Saleema Amershi and her colleagues at Microsoft describe their industrial-AI work as a nine-step pipeline. In it, step 6 (model training) might be called core AI

edges.target: Microsoft engineers ~10% time on core AI (Amershi et al.)
edges.ref: 8. S. Amershi et al., "Software engineering for machine learning: A case study," in Proc. 41st Int. Conf. Software Engineering: SEIP '19, pp. 291-300.
edges.evidence: according to Amershi, industrial-AI engineers at Microsoft spend only approximately 10% of their time working on core AI components

edges.target: Red Hat Kubernetes ML pipeline / role overlap (Benton)
edges.ref: 9. W. Benton, "Machine learning and discovery with Kubernetes," in Proc. Software Engineering Machine Learning Int. Symp., 2019.
edges.evidence: Red Hat engineer Bill Benton reports that when we look at these data-mining pipelines, there is much overlap between the activities of data scientists and people in more traditional roles

edges.ref: 10. F. Pedregosa et al., "Scikit-learn: Machine learning in Python," J. Mach. Learn. Res., vol. 12, pp. 2825-2830, Oct. 2011.
edges.evidence: 50 authors have pushed 119 commits to master ... 279 files. All of this is possible because scikit-learn uses state-of-the-art open source SE methods
edges.section: Rule 4: Better SE Leads to Better AI

edges.target: Open-closed principle in ML frameworks (Braiek, Khomh, Adams)
edges.ref: 11. H. B. Braiek, F. Khomh, and B. Adams, "The open-closed principle of modern machine learning frameworks," in Proc. 2018 IEEE/ACM 15th MSR, pp. 353-363.
edges.evidence: Their analysis is a nuanced discussion of what can go right and wrong when modern SE is applied to machine-learning tools. That said, their paper agrees

edges.target: Software-specific NL techniques / word frequency != importance (Binkley, Lawrie, Morrell)
edges.ref: 12. D. Binkley, D. Lawrie, and C. Morrell, "The need for software specific natural language techniques," Empir. Softw. Eng., vol. 23, no. 4, pp. 2398-2425, Aug. 2018.
edges.evidence: Dave Binkley and others note that text-mining methods for understanding software code often mistakenly equate word frequency with word importance
edges.section: Rule 5: SE Needs Special Kinds of AI

edges.target: Automated parameter optimization for defect prediction (Tantithamthavorn et al.)
edges.ref: 13. C. Tantithamthavorn, S. McIntosh, A. Hassan, and K. Matsumoto, "Automated parameter optimization of classification techniques for defect prediction model," ICSE 2016.
edges.evidence: such automatic tools can adjust the control parameters of, say, a data miner to greatly improve its predictive performance.13, 14

edges.target: Is AI different for SE? (Agrawal & Menzies, NCSU TR-2019-4)
edges.ref: 14. A. Agrawal and T. Menzies, "Is AI different for SE?" NC State Univ., Aug. 26, 2019. [Online].
edges.evidence: such automatic tools can adjust the control parameters of, say, a data miner to greatly improve its predictive performance.13, 14

edges.target: SE-specific sentiment analysis benchmark (Novielli, Girardi, Lanubile)
edges.ref: 15. N. Novielli, D. Girardi, and F. Lanubile, "Benchmark study on sentiment analysis for software engineering research," in Proc. 2018 IEEE/ACM 15th MSR.
edges.evidence: After retraining those tools on an SE corpus, they found better performance at predicting sentiment and more agreement between different sentiment tools.

edges.target: Naturalness of buggy code / n-gram language models (Ray, Hellendoorn, ... Devanbu)
edges.ref: 16. B. Ray, V. Hellendoorn, S. Godhane, Z. Tu, A. Bacchelli, and P. Devanbu, "On the 'naturalness' of buggy code," in Proc. 38th ICSE, 2016, pp. 428-439.
edges.evidence: the "naturalness" work of Prem Devanbu and his colleagues. Software has the property that some terms are used very often, and everything else is used with exponentially less frequency.

not_reuse_examples: Refs 1-5 (Czerwonka CODEMINE, Misirli defect predictors, Alshahwan Sapienz, Backes one-click formal methods, Abdessalem vision testing): listed only in Figure 2 as a sample of 'AI for SE' applications; motivational background, nothing adopted.
Ref 6 (Krall, Menzies, Davies, pilot landing mitigations): self-citation in Figure 2's list of AI-for-SE examples; background only, no result or method reused.
Andrew Ng January 2019 Twitter post (Figure 1): cited as evidence of industry interest; not a reference entry and not a reused result.
notes: Opinion column (IEEE Software 'SE for AI' editorial, ~4 pages, 16 refs); no experiments, so no executed/steppingstone/dataset edges; three figures (3,4,5) are reproduced from refs 7,8,9; scikit-learn commit stats come from GitHub rather than ref 10 (transitive).
